exposure: type of care provider (obstetrician vs. midwife)
maternal preference for less medical intervention
outcome: perception of being pressured to induce labor
cohort: The study participants were 2119 respondents to the Listening to Mothers in California survey who were planning to have a vaginal birth in 2016.
finding: Almost half of the respondents experienced an attempted labor induction, with 37% of these being elective, and attempted induction was significantly associated with a higher likelihood of cesarean birth, particularly following a failed attempt.
mod_finding: Cesarean birth was 1.51 times more likely with overall induction and 4.50 times more likely following a failed attempt at labor induction.
cross-section timing: Data was collected from a survey reflecting birth experiences in 2016.
